tasks.short: Match supplier invoices to orders, deliveries and approved agency hours, then record them in AFAS.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice arrives in Outlook or an agency portal.
steps: Find the supplier, purchase order and delivery confirmation or approved agency hours.
Compare invoice quantities, rates, VAT and totals with the supporting records.
Ask the site manager or agency to explain differences.
Complete the AFAS booking and attach the supporting documents.
Route the invoice through the required approval workflow.
drudgery: Opening several records to check the same invoice
Copying agency hours and rates between portals and Excel
Chasing missing delivery confirmations
today.time_sinks: Missing order references, late confirmations from shifts and inconsistent agency invoice layouts.

lenses.faster: Read UBL directly and extract PDF fields once. Compare invoice lines with approved orders, receipts or agency hours without retyping them.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice arrival starts duplicate checks and matching. Approved, exact matches are booked automatically; missing evidence and differences enter an exception queue.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice against approved hours and contracted rates across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Track recurring overcharges and missing confirmations by agency and site.
lenses.joy: Remove routine line comparisons and attachment hunting. Keep investigating meaningful differences and helping sites fix their ordering habits.
lenses.options: For a mismatch, show possible explanations such as a partial delivery, wrong rate or wrong week, with the supporting records. A person selects the explanation rather than accepting a guessed match.
lenses.altitude: Own the matching rules, tolerances and quality of supplier references. Improve the share processed without touch while checking for incorrect automatic matches.
reach: Prepare supplier discrepancy cases for the Accountant.
Maintain agency invoice control packs with HR Administration.
Provide committed-cost and unbilled-hours inputs to FP&A.

tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the goods or services were actually received, resolve disputes with site managers and agencies, and recognise suspicious supplier changes.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software handles structured orders, receipts, rates and exact matches. An llm_step can extract or explain PDF content, but extracted fields must pass arithmetic and reference checks; PDF exceptions require approval.

in_practice.trigger: A new invoice enters the AP mailbox or an approved agency export becomes available.
steps: Import UBL or extract PDF fields while retaining the original document and field references.
Check supplier identity, duplicate invoice keys, arithmetic and verified bank details.
Match lines to approved orders and receipts, or agency hours and effective contract rates.
Book authorised exact matches; route PDF uncertainty, rate differences and missing confirmations to a person.
Record the match evidence and approved g-rekening allocation for downstream payment preparation.
in_practice.human_gate: The Controller approves rule changes and tolerances. The bookkeeper approves uncertain PDF fields and exceptions; budget holders confirm receipt where evidence is missing. Bank payment release remains separately authorised.
systems: AFAS Profit, with invoice matching configured
data_needed: Invoice lines, supplier identifiers and original documents
Approved orders and receipt or service confirmations
Approved agency hours by worker reference, site and week
Effective agency rates and authorised g-rekening allocation
Supplier master data and approved matching tolerances
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice dossier and approval history, plus a controlled integration log containing source IDs, rule versions, match results and reviewer decisions.

evidence.claim: The digest's S1 reports line-level invoice capture and automatic booking and approval for one-to-one matches in Profit 8; it provides no Noordhaven match rate.
AFAS documents configurable matching, margins and exception statuses; eligibility depends on configuration.
Agency tax liability can be reduced through payment-behaviour statements, required records and payment of the relevant tax portion into a g-rekening.
The 65% labour saving and 2.4 times processing speed are unmeasured Noordhaven pilot hypotheses.

risks: An invoice matches an order even though delivery or service completion was never confirmed.
Broad tolerances or supplier defaults allow incorrect invoices through.
Agency hours and rate versions are incomplete or inconsistent.
A g-rekening split is treated as eliminating liability rather than limiting exposure.
research_questions: What proportion of invoices already passes AFAS matching without bookkeeper intervention?
Do all three sites record approved receipts or service confirmations before invoices arrive?
Can each agency supply invoice lines and approved hours with stable identifiers and effective rates?
Can a representative pilot achieve the proposed saving without increasing incorrect matches or payment exceptions?

tasks.short: Check debits, credits and totals in AFAS, and keep the supporting Excel schedules consistent.

today.trigger: Daily postings arrive or a control schedule needs updating.
steps: Review AP, AR and bank transactions in AFAS.
Export balances or transaction details for supporting Excel schedules.
Calculate totals and compare debit and credit amounts.
Investigate differences and prepare authorised corrections.
Save the checked schedule and evidence.
drudgery: Repeated exports and spreadsheet totals
Checking copied formulas
Re-entering figures already held in AFAS
today.time_sinks: Spreadsheet versions, stale extracts and differences between transaction-level records and manually maintained totals.

lenses.faster: Use live AFAS totals and controlled Excel queries instead of copying balances and rebuilding formulas. Run debit-credit and control-account checks automatically.
lenses.autonomous: Posting completion or a daily schedule starts the checks. Balanced, complete results are recorded automatically; failed controls create a review item.
lenses.ambitious: Check AP, AR and bank control totals every day rather than discovering accumulated differences at month end. Give the Accountant an early view of accounts that could delay close.
lenses.joy: Remove calculator work and spreadsheet maintenance. Keep understanding unusual balances and improving the controls.
lenses.options: Show balances by site, period and account with drill-down to the same source transactions. Compare current totals with the prior period without maintaining separate spreadsheets.
lenses.altitude: Design and maintain the control checks that prove the transaction totals are complete. Review failures and trends instead of recalculating every account.
reach: Prepare control-account schedules for the Accountant.
Maintain reconciled AP and AR inputs for the Controller.
Provide verified cash and outstanding-balance inputs to FP&A.

tasks.human_edge: Recognise a financially implausible balance even when the arithmetic agrees, and decide when a difference needs accounting judgement.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software is sufficient for arithmetic, approved account mappings and control totals. AI coding can help build the checks, but a language model should not calculate or invent accounting entries at runtime.

in_practice.trigger: A posting batch completes or the daily control schedule runs.
steps: Read AFAS transactions and balances with a timestamp and stable transaction IDs.
Calculate debit-credit totals and reconcile supporting schedules using fixed decimal arithmetic.
Check completeness, account mappings, duplicates and unexpected balances.
Publish passed controls and send failed checks to the bookkeeper with source links.
Apply only approved corrections and rerun the affected checks.
in_practice.human_gate: The Controller approves control definitions and materiality limits. A person approves corrective journals; successful arithmetic checks need no individual approval.
systems: Excel Power Query or a controlled calculation service
Power BI for next-day trend reporting
data_needed: AFAS transaction IDs, accounts, debit and credit amounts, periods and sites
Opening balances and control-account definitions
Approved mappings and control thresholds
Source timestamps and expected batch totals
in_practice.logs_to: A controlled financial check register in SharePoint, linked to AFAS transactions and any approved correcting journals.

evidence.claim: AFAS automatically generates journal entries when recognised bank transactions are processed.
Structured accounting totals and completeness checks can use deterministic calculations; Noordhaven's schedules and controls still need inspection.
The 60% labour saving and 2.2 times processing speed assume substantial spreadsheet maintenance remains today.

risks: Balanced debits and credits conceal an incorrect account or missing transaction.
A partial extract produces convincing but incomplete totals.
The nightly Power BI extract is mistaken for a live operational balance.
Automatic checks duplicate controls already running in AFAS and save little time.
research_questions: Which calculations are already automatic in AFAS, and which Excel steps still take human time?
Can every supporting schedule be reconciled to transaction IDs and a complete extraction timestamp?
Which historical errors would the proposed checks have detected?
Does the pilot reduce handling time without increasing audit adjustments?

tasks.short: Code invoices and receipts to the right account, VAT code, site and period in AFAS.

today.trigger: An invoice, credit note or receipt needs a financial classification.
steps: Read the document and identify its supplier, purpose and service period.
Look up earlier bookings, the chart of accounts and relevant coding guidance.
Select the ledger account, VAT treatment and site or cost centre.
Enter the booking and attach the document.
Resolve questions with the Accountant before finalising unusual items.
drudgery: Reading recurring invoice descriptions
Looking up the same prior bookings
Typing account and cost-centre codes
today.time_sinks: Mixed invoices, unclear service periods, unfamiliar suppliers and VAT exceptions.

lenses.faster: Extract document fields and propose coding from approved rules and comparable bookings. Present the source text beside each proposal so checking replaces searching and typing.
lenses.autonomous: Known structured transactions follow approved coding rules. Unstructured descriptions produce a proposal for approval, with unfamiliar VAT treatment and period allocation held for review.
lenses.ambitious: Apply consistent site and cost-centre coding to every relevant line. Give FP&A cleaner costs and the Controller fewer reclassifications at close.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive description reading and code entry. Keep solving unusual transactions and improving the coding guide.
lenses.options: For ambiguous spend, show a small set of valid account choices with the rule or precedent behind each. Show alternative period allocations when the service dates require judgement.
lenses.altitude: Maintain the coding policy and review the reasons people override proposals. Improve the system rather than repeatedly correcting the same supplier.
reach: Prepare reclassification proposals for the Accountant.
Maintain site-cost mappings used by FP&A.
Help the Controller analyse recurring coding errors.

tasks.human_edge: Determine the economic substance of an unusual transaction and recognise when historic coding is wrong or no longer appropriate.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step converts unstructured invoice descriptions into checkable coding proposals inside a deterministic booking workflow. Exact structured matches use deterministic_software; accounting policy, unfamiliar VAT treatment and material allocations stay with a person.

in_practice.trigger: A captured invoice or receipt reaches the coding queue.
steps: Read structured fields or extract document text with source references.
Apply approved supplier and order mappings before requesting any model proposal.
Propose valid ledger, VAT, site and period codes with supporting rules or comparable bookings.
Validate totals, allowed codes, open periods and mandatory dimensions.
Have the bookkeeper approve the proposal and escalate judgement items to the Accountant before posting.
in_practice.human_gate: Each model-generated coding proposal requires approval. Accountant review is required for unfamiliar VAT treatment, material accruals, capitalisation and new policy interpretations.
systems: An approved document extraction and language-model service
data_needed: Original documents and extracted fields
Chart of accounts and valid VAT codes
Site and cost-centre mappings
Approved coding examples and policy versions
Service dates and open accounting periods
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS booking dossier and a controlled proposal log recording source passages, rule or model version, proposed codes, overrides and approval.

evidence.claim: AFAS Scan & herken extracts PDF invoice information and supports supplier identification; incomplete recognition requires manual completion.

Zone & Co documents coding suggestions from supplier history for human review. Its Escalante Golf case reports invoice processing falling from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds in NetSuite, which does not establish an AFAS result.
evidence.source: [S4: Zone & Co AP automation and Escalante Golf case](https://www.zoneandco.com/articles/ai-in-ap-automation)

evidence.claim: The 55% labour saving and twofold processing speed are Noordhaven hypotheses, not results transferred from the vendor case.

risks: A model repeats incorrect historical coding or invents a policy explanation.
Supplier defaults conceal mixed purchases or incorrect site allocations.
Invoice text manipulates the model unless treated strictly as document data.
Sensitive receipt information enters an unapproved service or excessive logs.
research_questions: How often does coding require judgement rather than a supplier or order rule?
Are historical bookings accurate enough to serve as approved examples?
Can proposals identify their supporting document passage and policy without inventing evidence?
Does a pilot reduce handling time and month-end reclassifications while maintaining VAT accuracy?

tasks.short: Move approved subledger and agency-export entries into the AFAS general ledger without rekeying.

today.trigger: A journal batch or external financial export is ready for transfer.
steps: Collect the approved source batch from AFAS or a controlled export.
Check account mappings, period, site codes and control totals.
Import or journalise the batch into the general ledger.
Compare posted entries and totals with the source.
Retain the batch evidence and resolve rejected lines.
drudgery: Reshaping exports for imports
Copying account and site codes
Checking whether a batch has already been posted
today.time_sinks: Changing export formats, unmapped fields, rejected imports and manual batch tracking.

lenses.faster: Use configured AFAS journalisation and reusable import mappings. Remove spreadsheet reshaping and rekeying where these still occur.
lenses.autonomous: An approved batch starts a validated transfer with a unique batch key. Missing mappings, closed periods and total differences stop the batch before posting.
lenses.ambitious: Move approved external batches daily with complete traceability. Reduce the volume of transfer problems discovered during month close.
lenses.joy: Remove copy-and-paste work and repeated batch-total comparisons. Keep resolving mapping problems and improving integration reliability.
lenses.options: Preview the mapped entries and compare them with the prior mapping version before approving a change. Replay a failed batch in test mode without creating duplicate postings.
lenses.altitude: Own the transfer mappings, completeness controls and failed-batch queue. Monitor whether every approved source entry reaches the ledger exactly once.
reach: Prepare integration reconciliation schedules for the Accountant.
Support payroll-to-ledger transfer controls with the Payroll Specialist.
Maintain the Controller's posting-completeness evidence.

tasks.human_edge: Approve changes to account mappings and decide how to handle a source batch that conflicts with accounting policy or the close timetable.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software maps approved fields, checks totals and transfers batches. Existing AFAS journalisation should be used first; AI can help develop adapters but is unnecessary for the transfer itself.

in_practice.trigger: An approved source batch becomes available or a configured AFAS journalisation schedule runs.
steps: Read the approved batch and assign a stable source and batch key.
Validate schema, mappings, permissions, accounting period and control totals.
Journalise through AFAS or use an approved import route with duplicate protection.
Compare posted counts and totals with the source and quarantine rejected records.
Record completion or route a failed batch to the bookkeeper for resolution.
in_practice.human_gate: The Controller or Accountant approves new mappings and period exceptions. Valid batches using approved mappings run without individual review.
systems: AFAS Profit scheduled journalisation and approved import facilities
data_needed: Approved source entries and stable source IDs
Versioned account and site mappings
Batch counts and debit-credit totals
Open-period and authorisation settings
Previously processed batch keys
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS journal batches and a controlled integration register with source keys, mapping versions, totals, posting IDs and failures.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents scheduled daily journalisation of sales invoices, supporting native transfer rather than manual re-entry.
External batches can use deterministic mapping, duplicate protection and reconciliation, subject to available interfaces.
The 75% labour saving and 3.2 times processing speed depend on finding genuinely manual transfers; savings may be small if AFAS already handles them.

risks: A retry posts the same source batch twice.
A mapping error propagates across an entire batch.
A partial import is marked complete despite rejected records.
The opportunity is overstated because this O*NET task is already native AFAS functionality.
research_questions: Which transfers still require a person after existing AFAS journalisation is accounted for?
Do the agency portals provide stable exports or supported interfaces?
Can interrupted imports be retried without duplicate or missing entries?
Can every posted batch be reconciled back to approved source counts and totals?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, supplier and customer balances, and explain differences before month close.

today.trigger: Bank statements arrive, a supplier sends a statement or a close reconciliation is due.
steps: Import Rabobank statements and review AFAS matching results.
Compare unmatched lines, supplier statements and control-account balances.
Find invoices, remittance advice, credits or timing differences.
Prepare explanations and proposed corrections.
Obtain approval where required and retain reconciliation evidence.
drudgery: Searching payment descriptions for invoice references
Comparing long statement lists
Rewriting explanations for recurring timing differences
today.time_sinks: Combined payments, short payments, unidentified receipts and differences with incomplete supporting evidence.

lenses.faster: Improve existing AFAS bank rules and compare structured statements automatically. Use a document-reading step to extract remittance references and draft explanations for unmatched items.
lenses.autonomous: A bank import or statement receipt starts reconciliation. Exact authorised matches clear automatically; ambiguous matches and proposed adjustments remain in a review queue.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile daily and track how long differences remain unresolved. Give the Controller a continuously updated list of issues likely to delay close or distort cash forecasts.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive reference searches and statement comparisons. Keep resolving real discrepancies with customers, suppliers and colleagues.
lenses.options: Show possible invoice combinations, timing explanations and missing evidence for each unresolved amount. Distinguish a numerically possible match from one supported by remittance evidence.
lenses.altitude: Manage reconciliation rules and the ageing of unresolved differences. Improve reference quality and fix recurring causes at their source.
reach: Prepare balance-sheet reconciliation packs for the Accountant.
Give the Credit and Collections Officer verified unmatched-receipt cases.
Provide reconciled cash information to FP&A.

tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a genuine settlement from a convenient amount match and decide when to challenge a supplier or customer explanation.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software performs exact AFAS matching and balance comparisons. An agent_with_gate gathers authorised evidence and proposes explanations across documents; a person approves ambiguous allocations, write-offs and correcting entries.

in_practice.trigger: A new bank statement, supplier statement or scheduled reconciliation becomes available.
steps: Run AFAS bank matching with approved references and tolerances.
Compare unmatched items and control balances with complete, timestamped source records.
Extract remittance or statement references and assemble candidate explanations with evidence.
Have the bookkeeper approve ambiguous allocations and obtain Accountant approval for adjustments.
Record reconciliation status, unresolved owners and approved corrections.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine exact matches operate at autonomy 4. The overall reconciliation remains at autonomy 3 because ambiguous allocations, write-offs and journals need approval.
data_needed: Bank lines and opening and closing statement balances
Open AP and AR items and existing allocations
Supplier statements and customer remittance advice
Approved tolerances and write-off authority
Complete extraction timestamps and transaction IDs
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS allocation and journal history, linked to a SharePoint reconciliation register containing evidence, candidates, decisions and unresolved owners.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches bank lines using references, IBAN, invoice numbers and amount checks; unmatched lines require manual processing.
AFAS can match combined payments, including an oldest-first amount sum. Numerical agreement therefore does not itself prove the customer's intended allocation.
Evidence gathering and drafted discrepancy explanations are plausible extensions, but their accuracy in Noordhaven's records is untested.
The 55% labour saving and 1.9 times processing speed are provisional estimates.

risks: An amount-based match clears the wrong invoices.
Tolerance settings hide repeated short payments.
A plausible explanation is accepted without supporting evidence.
An unidentified receipt is misclassified, distorting DSO and the cash forecast.
research_questions: What are the current match rate, manual handling time and most common unmatched-item causes?
How often do combined-payment rules allocate receipts differently from remittance instructions?
Can each drafted explanation identify complete supporting evidence and explicitly flag missing records?
Does the pilot reduce unresolved items and close delays without increasing write-offs or audit adjustments?

tasks.short: Prepare checked hours, allowances and payroll accounting inputs for the Payroll Specialist.

today.trigger: The payroll input deadline approaches or a payroll correction is requested.
steps: Collect approved hours, allowances and expense inputs from the sites.
Check employee references, periods and duplicate submissions.
Compare inputs with relevant CAO rules and approved payroll instructions.
Send checked inputs and unresolved questions to the Payroll Specialist.
Reconcile the approved payroll journal and related control balances.
systems: AFAS Profit HR, payroll and finance
drudgery: Combining site spreadsheets
Checking repeated employee and period references
Chasing incomplete input lists
today.time_sinks: Late shift approvals, corrections across periods and unclear allowance eligibility under the two CAOs.

lenses.faster: Validate approved payroll inputs once against employee records and versioned CAO rules. Generate the Payroll Specialist's input file and finance reconciliation without repeated copying.
lenses.autonomous: Approved site inputs start validation and draft preparation. The Payroll Specialist approves each submission batch and retains responsibility for payroll calculation and release.
lenses.ambitious: Check every submitted shift input for missing approvals, duplicate hours and invalid allowance codes before cut-off. Provide earlier, reconciled payroll-cost inputs for the forecast.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet consolidation and repeated identifier checks. Keep helping site supervisors resolve incomplete inputs and understanding cost differences.
lenses.options: Show the effect of alternative interpretations of an unclear allowance to the Payroll Specialist, using explicit assumptions. Never choose an employee's entitlement from a model's preferred scenario.
lenses.altitude: Own payroll-input completeness and payroll-to-ledger controls. Improve handovers between shift supervisors, HR and Payroll.
reach: Prepare payroll control schedules for the Payroll Specialist.
Prepare payroll-to-ledger reconciliations for the Accountant.
Provide approved payroll-cost actuals and unresolved-input summaries to FP&A.

tasks.human_edge: Protect employee trust, recognise disputed entitlements and escalate CAO interpretation to the Payroll Specialist and HR.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software validates identifiers, approved hours, periods and explicit CAO mappings, then prepares a submission. A copilot may summarise questions, but pay entitlement, employee changes and payroll release remain human decisions.

in_practice.trigger: A site submits approved payroll inputs or the agreed payroll cut-off check runs.
steps: Read only approved inputs and the minimum necessary AFAS employee fields.
Validate identifiers, effective dates, duplicate entries and supervisor approval.
Apply versioned mappings approved by Payroll for each applicable CAO and flag ambiguous cases.
Prepare a checked input batch and exception summary for Payroll Specialist approval.
Reconcile the resulting approved payroll journal with payroll totals and finance control accounts.
in_practice.human_gate: The Payroll Specialist approves every input batch, CAO mapping change and payroll correction. The bookkeeper does not release payroll or decide disputed employee entitlements.
systems: AFAS Profit HR, payroll and finance
data_needed: Employee IDs, employment dates and applicable CAO references
Approved hours and allowance inputs
Effective, Payroll-approved code mappings
Payroll cut-off and correction rules
Approved payroll journal and control totals
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted AFAS payroll input and journal history, plus a payroll control register recording rule versions, approvals and exceptions without unnecessary personal detail.

evidence.claim: Structured payroll input validation and payroll-to-ledger reconciliation are plausible; the digest does not establish Noordhaven's exact input workflow.
Noordhaven's payroll-input controls require company-specific CAO mappings and Payroll approval; capabilities for an agency's own payroll cannot be assumed available to its client.
The 45% labour saving and 1.6 times processing speed depend on this work belonging to the bookkeeper rather than already being completed by Payroll.

risks: A warehouse CAO rule is applied to an employee covered by CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer, or vice versa.
Agency workers are incorrectly included in Noordhaven's employee payroll.
Late or unapproved hours are treated as final inputs.
Payroll data is exposed through excessive access or general-purpose model prompts.
New employee monitoring or AI decisions affecting employment expand the scope and require separate OR, privacy and EU AI Act assessment.
research_questions: Which payroll preparation steps actually belong to the three bookkeepers, and which already belong to Payroll or HR?
Are approved hours available with stable employee IDs and the applicable CAO and rule version?
Can the system reproduce historical inputs, including corrections and allowance exceptions, without changing entitlements?
Can access remain restricted to necessary fields while excluding medical details and Wet verbetering poortwachter case records?

tasks.short: Issue customer invoices and account statements from approved transport and warehousing charges.

today.trigger: Approved service quantities are ready for billing or an account statement is requested.
steps: Collect approved transport and warehousing quantities and the applicable customer rates.
Calculate charges, agreed surcharges, VAT and invoice totals.
Create and check the invoice or account statement in AFAS.
Send it through the approved customer channel.
Resolve rejected invoices and pass disputed balances to Credit and Collections.
drudgery: Combining service quantities and rate tables
Checking recurring calculations
Creating statements that repeat AFAS balances
today.time_sinks: Missing service approvals, customer-specific references, tariff changes and billing disputes.

lenses.faster: Calculate invoices from approved service records and effective contract rates. Generate account statements directly from current AFAS balances.
lenses.autonomous: Approved service data starts a billing run. Standard invoices pass fixed checks and are issued automatically; missing references, unusual charges and credits require review.
lenses.ambitious: Check every approved service record for an invoice or a documented reason it remains unbilled. Reduce billing delay and give FP&A a clearer view of revenue still awaiting invoicing.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated tariff calculations and statement preparation. Keep resolving customer billing problems and improving invoice clarity.
lenses.options: Show alternative customer-approved grouping formats, such as per shipment or per site, before changing a template. Compare billing schedules for their effect on administrative effort and invoice timing.
lenses.altitude: Own billing completeness, rate validity and invoice acceptance. Improve the service-to-cash process rather than assembling each invoice.
reach: Prepare verified account statements for Credit and Collections.
Provide unbilled-service schedules to the Accountant.
Provide billing-delay and revenue-completeness inputs to FP&A.

tasks.human_edge: Interpret disputed commercial terms, preserve customer relationships and recognise when an apparently valid charge should be investigated.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software calculates charges from approved quantities, rates and VAT rules and generates standard documents. Language models are unnecessary for financial calculations; commercial disputes and new contract interpretations require a person.

in_practice.trigger: Approved service records become billable or an authorised statement request arrives.
steps: Read approved service quantities, customer records and effective tariff versions.
Calculate charges using fixed rules and validate VAT, references, duplicates and billing completeness.
Generate invoices through configured AFAS billing or an approved import route.
Issue standard invoices and statements; hold exceptions and nonstandard credits for approval.
Record delivery results and reconcile each billed service record to its invoice.
in_practice.human_gate: Commercial owners approve rates and contract changes. The bookkeeper reviews exceptions; credits and concessions follow delegated authority. Standard validated invoices need no individual approval.
systems: AFAS Profit, with suitable billing functionality configured
Controlled Excel or approved service-data exports
Outlook or the configured invoice delivery channel
data_needed: Approved transport and warehousing service quantities
Customer contracts, tariff versions and surcharge rules
Customer purchase references and delivery preferences
Approved VAT mappings and invoice templates
Service-to-invoice links and live account balances
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice and customer dossiers, with a controlled billing log recording service IDs, tariff versions, validation results and delivery status.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports configured invoice numbering, journal settings, customer profiles and scheduled invoice generation; the relevant module and configuration must be confirmed.
Completeness checks linking approved services to invoices are plausible, but Noordhaven's service-data source is unspecified.
The 65% labour saving and 2.4 times processing speed assume approved service data and effective rates can be obtained reliably.

risks: An obsolete tariff or surcharge rule creates systematic overbilling or underbilling.
Incomplete service records make automated invoices incomplete.
A delivered email is mistaken for customer acceptance of the invoice.
An old balance produces an incorrect account statement.
Faster invoicing is assumed to reduce DSO even when disputes or collection practices remain the bottleneck.
research_questions: Where are approved transport and warehousing service quantities recorded, and can they be linked reliably to customers and invoices?
Are rates and surcharges versioned by effective date with a named commercial owner?
Does Noordhaven have the necessary AFAS billing functionality and reliable invoice delivery records?
Can a pilot reduce service-to-invoice delay and unbilled items without increasing credit notes or disputes?

tasks.short: Prepare purchase orders and employee expense reports with the right coding and approvals.

today.trigger: A colleague requests a purchase or submits an expense claim.
steps: Collect the purchase request, quotation or expense receipts.
Check supplier or employee details, business purpose and policy limits.
Calculate amounts and select the site, account and VAT proposal.
Prepare the purchase order or expense report.
Route it to the budget holder and resolve missing information.
drudgery: Typing details from quotations and receipts
Combining receipt totals
Finding the correct policy and approver
today.time_sinks: Unreadable receipts, incomplete business purposes, duplicate claims and purchases requested after the commitment was made.

lenses.faster: Extract quotation and receipt details into a checked draft. Apply fixed policy checks and route the document using the site and amount.
lenses.autonomous: Submission starts capture, duplicate checks and draft preparation. A complete draft reaches the authorised approver without the bookkeeper assembling it by hand.
lenses.ambitious: Capture purchase commitments before invoices arrive and check every expense claim against the current policy. Give FP&A earlier visibility of approved spend by site.
lenses.joy: Remove receipt typing, total checking and approver hunting. Keep helping colleagues resolve unusual claims and improve request quality.
lenses.options: For purchases, compare supplied quotations on total cost, delivery date and payment terms. For expenses, show compliant correction routes and the evidence needed for an exception.
lenses.altitude: Own the quality of purchase and expense submissions and the approval routing. Reduce recurring missing information and purchases made outside the agreed process.
reach: Prepare commitment schedules for FP&A.
Maintain purchasing documentation for budget holders.
Prepare checked reimbursement inputs for the Payroll Specialist.

tasks.human_edge: Assess unusual business purposes, challenge questionable claims respectfully and decide when a policy exception needs an authorised owner.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step extracts unstructured quotation and receipt details into a checkable draft. deterministic_software handles arithmetic, policy limits and routing; purchase commitments, reimbursements and policy exceptions require human approval.

in_practice.trigger: A purchase request or expense claim is submitted through the agreed intake route.
steps: Extract supplier or employee references, dates, amounts and descriptions with links to the source documents.
Check arithmetic, duplicate receipts, required evidence, policy limits and valid coding.
Prepare a purchase-order or expense-report draft and identify the authorised approver.
Have the requester confirm the draft and the budget holder approve the commitment or reimbursement.
Record the approved document in AFAS and route payroll-related reimbursements to Payroll where applicable.
in_practice.human_gate: The requester confirms extracted facts; the budget holder approves every purchase commitment or reimbursement. Accountant or Payroll review covers uncertain VAT treatment and CAO-related reimbursement questions.
systems: Excel where a controlled staging file is needed
data_needed: Purchase requests, quotations, receipts and business purposes
Current purchasing and expense policies
Supplier and employee references
Site, account and approval-authority mappings
Existing purchase orders and claims for duplicate checks
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS purchase and expense dossiers, with source documents, extracted fields, policy version, exception reason and approval history.

evidence.claim: The digest's S1 reports AI-supported expense processing in AFAS InSite; availability in Noordhaven's environment still needs confirmation.
Receipt and quotation extraction followed by deterministic checks is plausible, but this exact combined workflow is not documented for Noordhaven.
Large companies must pay qualifying small suppliers within a maximum 30-day term; purchasing checks should account for this requirement.
evidence.source: [Rijksoverheid: Payment terms for large companies and SMEs](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/actueel/nieuws/2023/07/06/ondernemers-moeten-te-lang-wachten-op-hun-geld)

evidence.claim: The 50% labour saving and 1.7 times processing speed are provisional and do not assume approvers respond faster.

risks: Receipt extraction misreads VAT, currencies or totals.
A draft purchase order is sent before approval and creates an unintended commitment.
Duplicate claims evade checks through altered images or references.
Personal receipt information is retained or shared more widely than needed under AVG/GDPR.
Automatic routing uses outdated approval limits or applies the wrong reimbursement policy.
research_questions: Which purchase-order and expense steps are already available in AFAS and which still require manual preparation?
Do policy limits, approval authorities and supplier payment terms exist as maintained structured rules?
Can extraction and duplicate checks handle representative receipts, foreign currencies and resubmitted claims accurately?
Does the pilot save handling time while preserving approval evidence and preventing premature purchase commitments?
